display_title: An okay paper but the novlety is not sufficient. Experimental results are not convincing, either.

content.title: An okay paper but the novlety is not sufficient. Experimental results are not convincing, either.
content.review:
Strength:
- This work proposes to train an encoder to cope with the well-trained StyleGAN. Neither tuning the latent nor optimizing the StyleGAN is required during testing, making the model inference efficient and elegant.

- Style mixing is naturally used to achieve diverse generations. Hierarchal variations are achieved by manipulating the coarse and fine features in W+ space.

- The generated results of conditional face synthesis are appealing due to the capacity of StyleGAN. The faces from sketch and semantic maps are photo-realistic.

Weakness:
- The proposed method uses an identity loss is induced by a face recognition network, namely AcrFace. Hence, this method is designed solely for face generation but not general image-to-image translation, which conflicts with the claim that pSp is "a generic image-to-image translation framework".

- This paper claims that "a novel StyleGAN encoder" is proposed. However, the architecture of the encoder is based on the Feature Pyramid Network. The used units are convolutions and LeakyReLU, which are both routine choices. Most importantly, the idea of using an encoder has been explored by ALAE. Hence, using an encoder for StyleGAN is not novel and cannot be regarded as a contribution.

- The encoder is optimized by minimizing the combination of the pixel-wise loss, perceptual loss, identity loss, and regularization that keeps latent vectors close to the average value. This setting simply puts four known losses together, but the weights differ significantly for different tasks (Supp A.1). It seems that significant efforts are needed to choose these weights. I suggest the authors provide more details on how to determine the hyper-parameters. Does a complete grid search is required?

- The experimental results are not convincing to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method. In the task of face frontalization, R&R significantly outperforms the proposed method, at least for the current metrics. Besides, neither mainstream evaluation metrics (e.g., rank-1 accuracy and true accept rate) nor datasets (e.g., LFW, IJBA, and MegaFace) are used.

- The overall visual quality is not significantly better than that of the competing methods. For instance, in Fig. 2, It seems that the results of IDInvert look more realistic. In Fig. 5, I prefer the results of R&R, especially when I zoom in to check the details.


Novelty: 
The novelty of this paper is marginal. ALAE has explored the idea of introducing an encoder to copy with StyleGAN. While  directly embedding real images into W+ space makes the inference process efficient, the encoder settings, e.g., the loss function and network architecture, are simply borrowed from prior works.

Presentation:
The writing is OK but still needs some improvements. For instance, Figures 2-5 should be more self-contained. I suggest the authors proofread the manuscript.

 
Contribution:
This paper proposes to train an encoder to learn how to embed images into the W+ space of StyleGAN. Neither tuning the latent nor optimizing the StyleGAN is required during testing, so the inference is very efficient. Besides, diverse generations can be achieved by applying style mixing in the W+ space.

However, the proposed framework lacks novelty in general. The claims like "(we propose) a novel StyleGAN encoder" and "we present a generic image-to-image translation framework" are not well supported.
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.confidence: 5: The reviewer is absolutely certain that the evaluation is correct and very familiar with the relevant literature

content.title: Comment on review
content.comment:
Thank you for taking the time to review the paper, we are happy to see you found the encoding method efficient and elegant and that you liked the idea of using style-mixing for multi-modality.

Let us try and address your concerns in the form of a Q&A:

### How can the method be generic if it uses an identity loss?
There might have been a misunderstanding as to what generic means. Unlike previous approaches that design an architecture for a sole task, such as frontalization, super-resolution, or inpainting, we present a single, generic solution that can handle all these tasks with only a change to four hyperparameters. 
We chose to work with the facial domain due to the large number of image-to-image translation tasks that are defined there, and we believe that it is an important domain on its own. In fact, the CVPR version of the original StyleGAN paper shows only results on facial images, even though the model supports other domains as well. With that being said, we have tested our method on other domains as well with promising results, and are planning to add some examples to our paper. For these other domains the identity loss is simply not used.

### How can the architecture be novel if it utilizes convolutions and LeakyRelus?
Clearly, we do not claim that we invented the building blocks here, but rather that we are using them in a way that hasn’t been applied before for StyleGAN encoding. Specifically, while feature pyramid networks are widely used for object detection, they haven’t been used for StyleGAN encoding, and we find our variant which routes different pyramid scales to different latents to be novel.

### Doesn’t setting the loss weights require a lot of effort?
We do not believe so, the paper utilizes four different loss functions, where the regularization loss is fixed at 0.005 and all the other losses have two or three possible values. Setting the values was done following the nature of each task, without the need for a full grid search. Taking into account that each of the mentioned tasks is usually solved using a completely new architecture, we are a bit confused that you deem setting three hyperparameters as challenging.


### The experimental results are not convincing, isn't the R&R method better?
Once again we note that the purpose of our method is to propose a single, unified, approach for solving these image-to-image translation tasks. While the state-of-the-art R&R presents better quantitative results it involves a substantially more complex pipeline including 3DMM model fitting, which is clearly not applicable to other tasks. We find the fact that our method can even compete with such a specialized method, while also being x10 faster, to be a strong point rather than a problem with our method. The ICLR guidelines clearly state that “Submissions bring value to the ICLR community when they convincingly demonstrate new, relevant, impactful knowledge. Submissions can achieve this without achieving state-of-the-art results.”, and we believe that this question clearly falls under this definition.


### The overall visual quality doesn’t seem better than previous approaches
We are surprised that you feel this way, as the visual quality is governed by the state-of-the-art StyleGAN method. Our human evaluation clearly shows the superiority of our approach for conditional image generation. As to other encoders, the visual quality is similar because they all utilize the StyleGAN model, the main difference there is in terms of reconstruction accuracy, as can be seen in Table 4a.


### Where is the paper’s novelty?
Hopefully, we’ve already addressed this concern in our previous answers, but let us try and address it again. We believe that the paper proposes two main novelties 
* `a novel StyleGAN encoder` - A new StyleGAN encoder that shows how one can utilize a feature pyramid network to map the different pyramid scales into StyleGAN, with a curated set of loss functions chosen for this task.
* `a generic image-to-image translation framework` - A framework that allows solving different image-to-image translation problems, such as frontalization and super-resolution using a unified pipeline.
It is important to note that while StyleGAN encoders were proposed in the past, they haven’t been utilized for direct image-to-image translation. Our core insight here is that one can directly encode the task into StyleGAN without the need for inversion beforehand, allowing one to support many new tasks such as conditional image generation and super-resolution. We believe that the ease-of-use of our approach will encourage further research into utilizing StyleGAN for real image-to-image tasks.

### Writing quality should be improved
While other reviewers noted that the paper is well written, we will try our best to address any points that were not clear.

content.title: Useful approach, good results, limited domain
content.review:
The paper proposes a new architecture for StyleGAN encoders. The proposed encoders output the high-dimensional representation in W+ vector space. The main encoder takes as an input a face image and outputs its latent code. There are additional encoders that take segmentation map, sketches, and a frontalizing encoder.

Pros:
-- The paper is well written, it has a thorough evaluation section.
-- A large number of applications show the versatility of the translation approach within the face editing domain
-- The results are really good, clearly an improvement over two strong competitors (ALAE and IDInvert). 
-- While the idea of latent-space editing is well-explored, the multimodal translation image translation ideas are new and interesting to me.
-- The proposed architecture of the encoder makes sense and is apparently working well.

Cons:
-- A single domain (near frontal faces) is considered
-- Most ideas behind the encoding part (the idea of training an encoder, the use of W+ space, the losses) have been proposed before.
-- As the authors rightfully admit in the discussion section, the whole approach works well whenever the target domain can be well covered by StyleGAN (e.g. near frontal faces). For most domains this is not true, and the proposed approach will not be competitive with more local image translation approaches (unless optimization and generator adjustment are added on top).
-- The idea behind the unsupervised frontalization is a bit hacky. The frontalization results are worse than for other applications.

content.title: Comment on review
content.comment:
Thank you for your review and insights, we have indeed put a lot of effort into the evaluation section to show that our method can generalize to a large number of applications. We are happy to see that you liked the idea of utilizing the latent-space for multi-modal translation, we found it to be one of the most interesting advantages of utilizing StyleGAN.

Let us try and address your concerns in the form of a Q&A:

### Why is only a single domain evaluated? Will the method generalize to other domains as well?
We decided to focus on the facial domain due to the wide variety of image-to-image translation problems that exist in that domain and we do not find that choice restrictive. In fact, the CVPR version of the original StyleGAN paper shows only results on facial images, even though the model supports other domains as well. 
With that being said, we have tested our method on other domains as well with promising results, and are planning to add some examples to our paper. While our method does require a pre-trained StyleGAN generator, recent papers such as “StyleGAN2 with adaptive discriminator augmentation” and “Few-Shot Adaptation of Generative Adversarial Networks” have shown that such a generator can be trained easily with much fewer examples than required in the past.
We do agree that the method isn’t the right solution for every image-to-image translation problem, and made it clear in our paper. Still, as you have noted in your review, we do show a wide variety of applicable problems.

### What is the novelty of the method compared to other StyleGAN encoders?
While the idea of using a StyleGAN encoder was proposed in recent prior works, we still believe our encoder to be novel. First of all, the proposed architecture, with the hierarchical style2map layers, is specifically designed for StyleGAN as noted in your review. Also, the identity loss and the regularization loss haven't been used in previous encoders.
We also wish to note that we find our major contribution to be the usage of the proposed StyleGAN encoder for image-to-image translation. This idea was not proposed in previous encoders, where editing tasks were defined as “invert first, edit later”. Our core insight here is that one can directly encode the task into StyleGAN without the need for inversion beforehand. This allows one to solve tasks where the input image is not represented in the StyleGAN domain.

### Isn’t the frontalization approach a bit hacky?
Actually, we believe it to be more elegant than hacky. The underlying idea here is that if we train the model to output both the original image and the mirrored one, the model converges to a frontalized result. As to the results, one has to remember they are obtained without any labeled frontal faces and using the same architecture as other tasks. Our method is also x10 faster than the state-of-the-art R&R method which uses a much more complex pipeline requiring both 3DMM fitting and a pix2pix model.

content.title: Learning Encoder for StyleGAN
content.review:
This paper provides a way to learn an encoder for a pre-trained StyleGAN. Given the structure of StyleGAN, the encoder is also designed to output different style codes in different layers. With a fixed StyleGAN as an image decoder, the author train the encoder with image reconstruction loss, perceptual loss, and face identity loss. Multiple experiments are performed on human face reconstruction and generation. 

Pros:

+ The method is simple and the qualitative results also look good. 
+ The authors also show that the encoder is able to use for training other image-to-image translation tasks besides reconstructing the original image. 
+ The method shows improvement over state-of-the-art approaches including SPADE and pix2pixHD quantitatively and qualitatively. 

Cons:
- Although the paper provides a simple method for training the StyleGAN encoder, the training processes of the encoder and StyleGAN are separated, there is no discussion on what happens if we train the StyleGAN and encoder together from scratch. This makes the comparison also a little unfair since pix2pix is an auto-encoder that can be trained end2end. 
- For a more fair comparison, there should be a baseline that also uses a pre-trained GAN and only train an encoder for the pre-trained GAN. 
- The authors only show results on human faces, which is a bit restricted. The loss also contains an identity loss which is designed for faces, which makes the method less generalizable. The authors should show results on other categories, for example, cars and birds. The author should also analyze how important the identity loss is.

content.title: Comment on review
content.comment:
Thank you very much for your evaluation. As mentioned in your review, we believe that one of the strong points of the proposed method is its extension to other image-to-image translation tasks besides reconstruction. Such an extension of StyleGAN hasn’t been proposed before and allows for a simple training scheme that is competitive with state-of-the-art approaches. 

Let us try and address your concerns in the form of a Q&A:

### Isn’t using a pretrained StyleGAN results in an unfair advantage over previous image-to-image methods?
You are correct that using the pretrained StyleGAN is one of the main advantages of our method, and it is well highlighted in our paper. However, we do not find it an unfair one. In fact, one of our main claims is that training an encoder to utilize a pretrained StyleGAN generator is a better approach for image-to-image translation, than training both the encoder and generator together.
As discussed in the paper, this approach would not work for every image-to-image problem. However, one can see that even for papers that handle only a specific application, such as face frontalization or conditional face generation, methods still try to build upon a general pix2pix network, instead of utilizing a pretrained GAN, and therefore have to resort to complex architectural changes and loss functions that do not generalize to other tasks.


### Why are the results only presented on facial images?
The facial domain is one of the most evaluated domains for image-to-image translation problems and GANs and we therefore do not find our choice to focus on that domain as restrictive. In fact, the CVPR version of the original StyleGAN paper shows only results on facial images, even though the model supports other domains as well. 
With that being said, we have tested our method on other domains as well with promising results, and are planning to add some examples to our paper. As to the usage of identity loss, the paper shows that this is a crucial addition for facial encoding due to the challenge of preserving identity information in the encoding process, as can be seen in Figure 3b. For other domains we have seen that our method can generalize well even without the identity loss and therefore we do not find it restrictive as well.

content.title: General Comment
content.comment: Dear reviewers, we would like to thank you for taking the time to read and evaluate our paper.  We hope that your remarks and insights will help us to refine our paper and make it clearer to its future readers. While the reviews were generally positive, we believe they do not fully reflect our paper and will therefore reconsider whether ICLR is a suitable match for our submission.
